desk.headline: Adjusted revenue up 10% to $84.4m, beat; 2026 services revenue range trimmed at the top, $300m buyback
results: Adjusted revenue, Bullish's main revenue measure, rose 10% to $84.4m, above the $80.2m analysts expected.
Subscription, services and other revenue grew 13% to $56.3m, while trading-related (adjusted transaction) revenue rose about 5% to $28.0m.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 24% to $35.6m, a 42% margin; adjusted net income was $18.7m against $13.8m.
Reported net income jumped to $576.3m ($3.57 a diluted share) mainly on a $598.4m gain in the value of digital assets held; the nine months still show a $308.6m loss.
Digital asset sales fell to $32.1bn from $41.6bn; the board approved a share buyback of up to $300m.

guidance.summary: Bullish cut the top of its 2026 subscription, services and other revenue range to $225–235m (was $225–245m). It now sees lower adjusted operating costs of $220–225m but higher finance expense of $60–65m.

points: CEO Tom Farley described a deep crypto bear market and said US growth since the IPO has been weaker than he expected.
The Equiniti purchase has antitrust clearance and is expected to close in early January 2027; targeted medium-term net cost savings were raised to $75–100m from $25–50m.
Bullish began booking tokenization revenue from several customers in Q4, mostly equities, but management called the pace of issuer adoption the biggest open question.
Management said it sees the shares as undervalued; buybacks will start only after extra financial filings with the SEC in the week of 30 Nov.
A US derivatives launch is expected within the next several months, depending on regulators.
call.source: Call coverage — MarketBeat (via Yahoo Finance) and The Block, 18 Nov 2026; prior outlook from the Q2 2026 release (13 Aug 2026)

watch: Closing of the Equiniti deal in January and how quickly issuers adopt tokenized shares.
Whether trading volumes and transaction revenue recover from the weak crypto market in Q4.
Timing and size of buybacks under the new $300m authorisation.
